_comment: BUILD_PLAN D1 — declared harm bound levels. USER DECISION, 2026-07-31.
Every level in research/HARM_MODEL_DRAFT.md was 'TBD — user decision';
these are the first declared values. They are deliberately TIGHT: the
point of D1 is a declared, falsifiable model, and tightening later is
cheap while loosening after a loss is not.
H1_credits: max net drawdown per run, in credits. The quantity may be
negative by design (net debt is never clamped, wallet.py:276-280), so
this is a floor on net position, not a cap on magnitude.
H2_market_capital: same shape. NOTE the standing hazard: _capital is a
mutable dict no gate reads (market.py:231, mutated :287/:325/:332/:345).
This bound makes the exposure measurable; it does NOT fix the
representation. The fix is to route market P&L through LedgerEntry.
H4_authority: 0. Authority exceedance is a BREACH, not a budget — the
attenuation theorem says it cannot happen, so any count above zero is a
broken invariant rather than consumed allowance.
C-8: this file will move into the signed guard-configuration trust domain.
Until then it is an ordinary repo file and is NOT tamper-evident.

H5_storage_growth: 1e10 bytes = 10 GB. NOT a level invented here -- it is transcribed from GyzaConfig.max_artifact_store_gb, which the operator had already declared and which nothing read (it was printed by `gyza status` as an enforced cap while ArtifactStore.max_bytes stayed None everywhere).

H6_unsupervised_actions: 10000. THE REVIEW CADENCE, chosen by the operator 2026-08-15: how many signed actions may occur before a human looks. Stated in actions rather than credits because TOKEN_IS_FAKE -- a credit bound cannot be checked against anything, an action count can.

H1_credits RETIRED 2026-08-15 (user decision): credits are TOKEN_IS_FAKE, so no level in them is checkable. It is listed in UNMODELLED so the gap is visible rather than absent. Autonomy is bounded by H6 in actions instead.

H2_market_capital RETIRED 2026-08-17 (owner decision): BondedMarket has zero production constructors and gates.py passes capital_entries=[], so the class measured 0.0 in every production evaluation. Listed in UNMODELLED. NOTE: removing a bound is a TIGHTENING, not a loosening -- an unset bound FAILS CLOSED, so a class with no bound admits nothing (guardconfig.diff_bounds).
v2, 2026-08-21 — H6_unsupervised_actions MOVED from `bounds` to `policy`.
It is a review CADENCE, not a harm bound. Its quantity is the count of
signed envelopes, and an adversary doing harmful work signs exactly as
many as a benign agent doing useful work (R-EVID Part B: evidence 0), so
the level asserted only that the agent had not yet run 10,000 actions.
A timer is exactly what a cadence should be; the mechanism was always
correct and only the classification was wrong. The INTERVAL IS UNCHANGED
at 10,000 and is still signed by the same authority — what changed is
that it no longer claims to bound harm, and no longer blocks the
containment claim by being a bounded-but-timer class.
Removing a key from `bounds` is classified TIGHTENED by diff_bounds (an
unbounded class fails closed and admits nothing), so this installs
without a LooseningRecord — correctly, since nothing loosened.
v3, 2026-08-21 — H3_mesh_exit_rate DECLARED at 300,000,000 bytes per
trailing hour, per node. USER DECISION (Aaron), informed by measurement
and not determined by it.
MEASURED BASIS. A saturated benign node emits 2,969 B/action: 1,077 from
the inference call (R-EVID Part B, production _executor) and 1,892 from
gossip deltas (research/evidence/measure_peer_egress.py, two live daemons
on loopback). At the measured 305 ms/action sandbox ceiling that is
35.0 MB/h per core, so 300 MB/h covers a SATURATED 8-core node at 1.07x
and a 4-core node at 2.14x. Larger nodes must raise it deliberately,
which is a signed and attributable act rather than a default.
WHY A RATE AND NOT A TOTAL. Mesh exit is irreversible, so bounding it by
capacity is unavailable in principle — nothing un-sends. A cumulative
byte budget is a TIMER: it refuses every benign node at ceil(L/b)
(R-EVID Theorem 2). A trailing wall-clock window supplies the
compensation term the fold needs, and the origin advances with TIME and
nothing else, so an agent buys egress budget by waiting and never by
acting — the distinction from ledger artifact #13.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT BOUND, stated because the level would otherwise be
read as stronger than it is: a rate bounds the RATE, never the TOTAL.
Unbounded operating time still permits unbounded total exit. And
0% of the measured egress is reducible by wiring attestation —
is_attestable_channel is true for send_message alone, so gossip and DHT
traffic can never be reclassified out of the exit count. The 'H3 shrinks
as the mesh grows' property is gated on SETTLEMENT traffic existing, not
on the mesh growing.
diff_bounds classifies ADDING a bound as a LOOSENING (an unbounded class
fails closed and admits nothing, so refuse-all -> admit-some). This is
the first declared level for a measured-not-bounded class, declared by
the authority holder as a deliberate act, and recorded here as one.

H7_irreversible_actions = 0 (2026-08-24, UNSIGNED DEV STATE). 0 is the only level that is a BOUND rather than a timer: benign drift is exactly 0 under a grant with no network and no writes outside an append-only store, and strictly positive under any other grant. This file is the honest development state; the SIGNED configuration still lacks H7, so `gyza status` with an authority key correctly reports the class UNBOUNDED and can_claim_containment FALSE until the owner signs guard_bounds.v4.draft.json. See research/IRREVERSIBILITY.md.
